subject.title: Model configuration accepts unvalidated model names, enabling silent misconfiguration

question: Should OpenClaw warn for catalog-absent configured model refs by default, and what exception model should preserve custom or forward-compatible providers?
rationale: Current code intentionally keeps configured refs usable before they appear in live catalogs, so the remaining fix depends on maintainer intent for advisory versus strict validation and catalog trust boundaries.

options.title: Advisory catalog warnings
options.body: Warn in `config validate` and `doctor` for configured refs absent from trusted catalog evidence while preserving custom or forward-compatible refs through explicit intent or suppression paths.

options.title: Strict validation
options.body: Reject unknown configured refs during validation or config writes, which catches mistakes earlier but needs a compatibility and migration policy for existing custom setups.

options.title: Runtime-only diagnostics
options.body: Keep config permissive and rely on runtime unknown-model and fallback notices, accepting that bad refs remain discoverable only after use.

recommendation.title: Advisory catalog warnings
recommendation.body: Warn in `config validate` and `doctor` for configured refs absent from trusted catalog evidence while preserving custom or forward-compatible refs through explicit intent or suppression paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent model-selection and provider-identity history makes this the best available owner for the product-direction choice.
